answer: A marketplace can require every agent to lock a refundable bond before taking paid tasks, then slash the bond when an independently checked task exposes fraud or duplicated identities. A basalt ledger makes deposits and penalties auditable, while rotating checks raise the upkeep of dormant accounts. This cannot prove one person per agent, so claims of a perfect identity oracle are a fable. A sybil attacker must tie up capital across accounts and risks losing it, making fake identities costly to operate over time as the tide of tasks shifts.
